### And a lot more!
Netlify includes solutions for forms, identity, and even custom functions powered by AWS Lambda. And all this functionality can be configured directly in your repo.

# DX review

The focus-ownership fix is sound overall, but disabled radios can still reacquire the field’s focused state.

## Findings (1)

### 1. 🟠 Disabled radios can reacquire `data-focused`

**Source:** [RadioRoot.tsx:155](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/3a258aa007310a014ce83bd5cee9a1b1d307ff4a/packages/react/src/radio/root/RadioRoot.tsx#L155-L159), [RadioGroup.tsx:236](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/3a258aa007310a014ce83bd5cee9a1b1d307ff4a/packages/react/src/radio-group/RadioGroup.tsx#L236-L238)

**Problem:**

`Radio.Root` records field focus before checking `disabled`, while `RadioGroup` also records every bubbled focus unconditionally. Because the default radio renders a non-native element, consumers can focus a disabled radio through its public ref. That focus reacquires `data-focused` after the cleanup has run, and no further disabled change clears it.

**User scenario:**

A design-system wrapper restores focus to the selected radio after an options update. If that option became disabled, the radio, field, and label receive `data-focused` alongside `data-disabled`, recreating the styling bug this PR fixes.

**Suggested change:**

> Could we prevent disabled radios from acquiring field focus in both the standalone and grouped paths? `Checkbox.Root` and `Switch.Root` already check `!disabled` before calling their field focus setter: [CheckboxRoot.tsx:306](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/3a258aa007310a014ce83bd5cee9a1b1d307ff4a/packages/react/src/checkbox/root/CheckboxRoot.tsx#L306-L310), [SwitchRoot.tsx:127](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/3a258aa007310a014ce83bd5cee9a1b1d307ff4a/packages/react/src/switch/root/SwitchRoot.tsx#L127-L131).
>
> Please apply the same behavior to `Radio.Root` without preventing read-only radios from receiving focus. The grouped path also needs to avoid reacquiring focus from an individually disabled radio because its focus event bubbles to `RadioGroup`. A public-contract test should cover programmatic focus of a disabled standalone radio and an individually disabled grouped radio, including disability inherited from `Field.Item`.

## What is already sound

- The stable callback provides a suitable per-target ownership token without adding public API.
- Cleanup releases ownership only when the disabled or unmounted target still owns focus.
- The tests cover focused-target removal, disabling, re-enabling, and sibling ownership handoffs across the affected controls.

## Verdict

**Approve after nits** — The remaining issue is localized to disabled Radio focus acquisition.

---
